clue.text: One with hesitation hiding behind school platform

indicators.note: hiding behind places the following letters after the school in the answer

parts.note: a pod is a school of whales or dolphins
the Roman numeral for one is I
um is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone hesitant lurks behind the school stage, nervous about speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' is not a place of learning but a group of whales: POD.
explanation.definitionFit: A podium is a raised stand that a speaker or conductor stands on.

clue.text: Male in charge restricted by Europeans arguing

indicators.note: restricted by says the male-in-charge letters are hemmed in on both sides by the Europeans

parts.note: Poles are people from Poland

explanation.surface: A man in charge is hemmed in by quarrelling Europeans.
explanation.definitionFit: Polemics is the practice of disputation, so it is arguing as a noun activity.

clue.text: Swirling on ice, mad person devil- possessed

indicators.note: swirling suggests things spun about, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A skater whirling madly on the ice looks like someone possessed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swirling' rearranges ON ICE MAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A demoniac is someone believed to be inhabited by an evil spirit.

clue.text: Part of spectrum impinging on each part of viewer

indicators.note: impinging on puts the spectrum letters up against the following letters in sequence

parts.note: UV, ultraviolet, is part of the light spectrum

explanation.surface: A band of light strikes each part of an observer's eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'viewer' is cryptic for an eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The uvea is the pigmented middle layer of the eye, and an eye is what does the viewing.

clue.text: Secular Scot who won't fight?

parts.note: civil means secular, as in a civil rather than religious wedding
Ian is a typically Scottish first name

explanation.surface: A non-religious Scotsman who refuses to take up arms.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the tail phrase, describing a non-combatant.
explanation.definitionFit: A civilian is someone not in the armed forces, so not a combatant.

clue.text: The Italian desire to take part, for example

parts.note: il is the Italian for the
lust is strong desire
a ration is a portion or share, a part

explanation.surface: An Italian keen to join in, by way of example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take' and 'for' only link the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An illustration is an instance given to clarify a point, i.e. an example.

clue.text: We came to see — what's to see?

definitions.text: We came to see — what's to see?

parts.words: We came to see — what's to see?
parts.note: the question asks what grammatical form the phrase 'to see' takes in the sentence

explanation.surface: Tourists arrive and wonder whether there is anything worth looking at.
explanation.walkthrough: The grammar term for 'to see' is the answer; the sightseeing picture misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar the base form of a verb with 'to', such as 'to see', is called by this name.

clue.text: Pieces of music favoured, uplifting kind

parts.note: in means in favour, fashionable

indicators.note: in a down clue uplifting means the word for kind is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a sort is a kind

explanation.surface: Favourite musical pieces that are of a cheering sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' turns SORT upward to TROS.
explanation.definitionFit: Intros are the opening passages of songs, short pieces of music.

clue.text: Plant one pet apparently needs?

indicators.note: needs says the following words require, and so contain, the plant within their letters

explanation.surface: A plant that a pet apparently cannot do without.
explanation.walkthrough: The plant runs through 'one pet apparently'; it is catmint, which a pet cat craves, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepeta is the botanical genus of catmint, a garden plant.

clue.text: A short distance back and favourite is one hanging on

indicators.note: back means the short-distance word is read in reverse

parts.note: a mil is a thousandth of an inch, a very short distance
a pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: A favourite clings on, having dropped back a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns MIL into LIM.
explanation.definitionFit: A limpet is a shellfish famous for clinging tightly to rocks.

clue.text: Edgy situation with Richard's disc at number one?

parts.note: Cliff Richard is a British pop singer, so Richard's first name is Cliff
a record at number one is top of the charts

explanation.surface: A tense moment for Cliff Richard as his record reaches the top of the charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edgy' is literal: a place at the edge of a cliff. Cliff Richard is a veteran British pop singer.
explanation.definitionFit: A clifftop is a location right at the edge, so literally an edgy position.

clue.text: Religious building in independent school — right to be quiet

indicators.note: to be says the right letter is to become the quiet one

parts.note: Charterhouse is an English public (fee-paying) school in Surrey
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A church building inside a private school where one must keep silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' swaps the first R of CHARTERHOUSE for P. Charterhouse is a famous English fee-paying school.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapter house is a building attached to a cathedral where the clergy meet.

clue.text: Unusual Somalian exhibit in Paris

indicators.note: unusual says the letters of the word that follows are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A rare Somali artefact is on show in the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' rearranges SOMALIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo's famous portrait hangs in the Louvre in Paris, its most celebrated exhibit.

clue.text: President has, at home, disease diminishing to nothing

parts.note: in means at home
gout is a disease of the joints

explanation.surface: The president, staying at home, has an illness that is fading away.
explanation.definitionFit: Phasing out means gradually reducing something until it stops entirely.

clue.text: Coronet had to be specially made — a solid multi-faceted thing

indicators.note: specially made suggests the letters of the words before are refashioned into something new

explanation.surface: A crown needed custom crafting, an object with many facets like a gem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be specially made' rearranges CORONET HAD.
explanation.definitionFit: An octahedron is a solid geometric figure with eight faces.

clue.text: Mineral crushed in holy practice

indicators.note: crushed says the letters of the following words are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A mineral ground up as part of a sacred ritual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crushed' rearranges HOLY PRACTICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Chalcopyrite is a copper iron sulphide, the main ore of copper.

clue.text: Careless fielders — how stupid, on reflection

parts.note: slips are cricket fielding positions beside the wicketkeeper, and the fielders in them

indicators.note: on reflection says the exclamation is mirrored, read backwards

parts.note: doh is an exclamation meaning how stupid

explanation.surface: Sloppy fielders realise afterwards how foolish they were.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' turns DOH into HOD. Slips are close catching positions in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Slipshod describes work done carelessly and without attention to detail.

clue.text: Avidity of head after expression of sorrow

indicators.note: after places the headland after the lament

parts.note: to keen is to wail in mourning, a keen being a lament
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: A boss's eagerness following an outpouring of grief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' reads as a person in charge, but here it is a headland; 'after' sets it behind the lament, which is a verb-turned-noun from Irish mourning wails.
explanation.definitionFit: Keenness is eagerness, and avidity is enthusiastic eagerness.

clue.text: Destiny that's yet to be sealed, learner having probed nasty Arkansan city?

indicators.note: to be sealed says the word yet is enclosed by the destiny word

parts.note: fate is destiny

indicators.note: having probed says the learner letter pokes inside the nasty word

parts.note: vile means nasty
L is the learner sign on cars

explanation.surface: A fate not yet decided, with a novice poking into something nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be sealed' and 'having probed' are both container signals. The question mark flags that the city is only one example of an Arkansan city.
explanation.definitionFit: Fayetteville is a city in the US state of Arkansas, home of its main university.

clue.text: Viewer's confused by a colour with something circular unseen

indicators.note: confused says the letters of a colour are muddled into a new order
unseen says the circular letter is gone from the mix

parts.note: the letter O is circular in shape

explanation.surface: An observer is puzzled by a hue in which something round has vanished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges A COLOUR once 'unseen' removes one O.
explanation.definitionFit: Ocular means relating to the eye, so belonging to the organ that views.

clue.text: Marsupial with power, huge problem

parts.note: OS, outsize, is a clothing label meaning huge
a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: A powerful marsupial facing an enormous difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: OS stands for outsize, a clothing size.
explanation.definitionFit: A possum is an Australian or American pouched mammal, a kind of marsupial.

clue.text: Satanic indication at ground level?

parts.note: the devil is pictured with split feet, which mark where he stands on the ground

explanation.surface: A sign of the Devil seen at the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: The Devil is traditionally drawn with split hooves, the sign of him found at his feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A split hoof is the traditional mark of Satan, betraying his presence.

clue.text: Like a bit of propaganda given page in newspaper

indicators.note: in says the page letter sits inside the newspaper

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

explanation.surface: Propaganda gets a page in a tabloid.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: Spin is biased presentation of news, so propaganda that has been spun is given a slant.

clue.text: See 12
Shiny component of Lulu's trousers

indicators.note: component of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A singer's glittering trousers catch the light.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustrous means having a sheen or glow, so gleaming and bright.

clue.text: End of meal, one with maybe twice- pared Stilton and fruit

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the meal

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: twice pared says the cheese word is trimmed of its tail two times

parts.note: Stilton is an English blue cheese, so maybe signals it as an example of cheese

explanation.surface: Finishing a meal with a fruit and a trimmed piece of Stilton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice- pared' cuts two letters off the end of CHEESE, leaving CHEE; 'maybe' marks Stilton as an example of cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: The lichee, or lychee, is a sweet Chinese fruit with a scaly skin.

clue.text: Message about needing to look after top lady

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to mind is to look after
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen, the top lady

explanation.surface: A note concerning the need to care for a woman in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A reminder is a note sent to prompt someone's memory.

clue.text: Sailor goes to underworld in magical mode of transport

parts.note: a tar is an old word for a sailor
Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and his realm

explanation.surface: A sailor descends to the underworld on some enchanted vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: The TARDIS is the Doctor's time machine in the British TV series Doctor Who.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tardis is the time-travelling police box that carries the Doctor, a fantastical vehicle.
